thesis: Park National (NYSE: PRK), Q3 2026 10-Q filed 2026-11-05 (balance sheet, nonperforming table, capital ratios, merger note, efficiency/NIM excerpts read; full MD&A, deposit mix, CRE concentration unread). Acquired First Citizens (Tennessee-region, merger effective 2026-01-31; 1,988,131 shares issued, valued 324.1M), lifting assets from 9.81B to 12.65B, loans 8.05B to 9.77B, deposits 8.24B to 10.62B; goodwill 268.3M and intangibles 35.1M. Q3 NI 56.9M vs 47.2M (+20.7%), 9M 157.4M vs 137.4M; TTM NI (FY25 180.1M + 9M26 - 9M25) 200.0M. Shares 18,070,328 (cover 2026-11-04) x 171.89 (2026-11-17 close) = market cap 3,106M = 15.5x TTM NI (TTM holds only 8 months of the acquired bank, so this is overstated vs a run rate; 9M annualized 209.8M gives 14.8x, not definitive). Book equity 1,713.0M = 1.81x; tangible equity 1,409.6M = 2.20x TBV (TBV/share 78.0). Dividend 1.10 quarterly = 2.56% yield. Credit: ACL 109.9M vs loans 9,772.9M (1.12%); nonperforming loans 90.4M (0.92% of loans) vs 69.3M at year-end; OREO 18.6M vs 0.7M. Capital: CET1 13.88%, total risk based 15.06% (holding company). NIM 4.82% 9M. Reported efficiency 60.5% (adjusted 56.4%).
counterthesis: Paying 2.2x tangible book and about 15x earnings for a regional bank leaves little room for credit or integration error. NPLs rose 31% in nine months and OREO rose to 18.6M, partly from acquired assets. AOCI loss widened to 69.7M from 12.7M. Efficiency worsened to 60.5% from 57.0% on merger costs (about 9.4M salaries in 9M) and the new region's cost base. Share count rose by about 12% through the deal, diluting per-share growth; PNB-level leverage ratio 10.55% and CET1 12.29% are tighter than holding-company figures. CRE exposure, uninsured deposits and the funding mix after the deal were not read.
invalidation: Thesis fails if nonperforming loans exceed about 1.5% of loans, NIM compresses below about 4.3%, adjusted efficiency stays above 58%, or integration of the acquired franchise leads to deposit attrition.
